_meta.purpose: WP2 incident inventory for results/framework/supervision_bench. Every case here is a CANDIDATE bundle; the export tool must verify artifact survival before promoting a case to raw.
sources_read: figures_data.json (for job ids and per-run numbers)
the research-evidence reader report (used as an index, then verified against the primary sources)
_meta.path_convention: artifact_paths_expected are relative to the cluster repo root unless they start with ~ or uploads/ (lab server) or are an explicit sacct/journalctl command.
_meta.unverified: No cluster or lab-server access was used. Every artifact path is a prediction derived from the #SBATCH --output line of the script that produced the job, and every provenance_guess is a judgement, not an observation.
_meta.scope_note: scope=cluster-pipeline and scope=campaign-governance are proposed for the benchmark. scope=platform-ui and scope=robot-uplink are inventoried for completeness because the record names them as concrete failures, but they have no /ocean artifacts and no supervision-loop bundle; they are excluded from both splits.

cases.one_line_symptom: Qwen-7B never produced a parseable action; 30 consecutive fallback-pipeline calls, no training, no evaluation.
cases.root_cause: Free-text JSON action contract with no native tool-calling; the model can generate prose but not the schema.
cases.correction_made: Ollama native function calling added as a backend (brain.py three-backend design).

cases.correction_made: BRAIN_STRICT default-on in run_v3_0_43_brain_harvest_oneshot.sh; both zero-label sets quarantined with their measured reason.
detectable_from: per-download labelled and class counts in the harvest log
registry entries with local_labeled 0
cases.provenance_reason: round 1's collect .out is a campaign artifact and the quarantine reasons are in the registry.
cases.notes: Subject-agnostic usable-labels beat every vocabulary; this is the correction a supervisor limited to config could actually have made.

cases.title: The scheduler was about to attach a day-old number to a fresh round
cases.one_line_symptom: The round's training wrote to mega_iterm1_curated_s101/train2 while train/ still held the previous day's M1 run; _train_metric globbed the plain train path and would have published 0.5873 from 04:52 as the result of a round that started at 15:05.
cases.root_cause: Ultralytics increments the run directory and the reader took a fixed path, with no freshness or ownership check.
cases.correction_made: _train_metric(started_ts) takes the newest results.csv under mega_iter*/train*/ and accepts it only if written after the step started, otherwise logs the refusal and attaches no metric. WP1 later replaced this with a job-scoped artifact read by job id.
detectable_from: results.csv mtime against the step start time
two sibling run directories under one mega_iter
cases.provenance_reason: both run directories are named in the record and were still present when the scheduler read them.
cases.notes: Canonical stale_artifact fixture: the two mtimes are the whole case.

cases.title: A dashboard restart orphaned a live 2 h 40 m training job and freed the scheduler to submit it again
cases.one_line_symptom: In-process _STATE was lost on restart; the ledger still showed the step running but the scheduler no longer knew about it.
cases.root_cause: Scheduler state lived only in process memory while the durable truth was on the ledger.
cases.correction_made: _recover_inflight() re-adopts any step still marked running with its real job id at mount; verified in the service log for job 44278259.
detectable_from: a ledger step marked running with no in-process owner after a restart
squeue showing a job the scheduler does not track
cases.provenance_reason: the evidence is a lab-server journal line plus the scheduler state file.

cases.title: A new measurement tool reported 15,789 labelled images against a real 120,515
cases.one_line_symptom: The pool report read a flat 0 for cottonweed_sp8, the in-domain core the merge trains on every round.
cases.root_cause: It read the registry field local_labeled, which only later harvests populate; legacy entries report 0.
cases.correction_made: Count label files on disk, bounded to labels* directories and never descending into image trees.
detectable_from: a per-source labelled count of 0 for a source known to be labelled
cases.provenance_reason: pool_report.json is synced to the lab and read by the Evidence panel.
cases.notes: The tool caught an error in itself on its first run; a good instrument-calibration control.

cases.title: The platform had been serving a 2026-08-18 registry: the cluster sync had been hung since 2026-08-03
cases.one_line_symptom: Quarantine badges rendered empty because the dashboard's registry had 60 datasets and no governance fields; ps showed one rsync alive for 20 days 18 hours.
cases.root_cause: A blocked ssh; systemd will not start a new run while the old one lives, so the timer simply stopped without ever reporting a failure. The recorded cause (a stale askpass password) was a guess.
cases.correction_made: Process killed, service restarted, registry re-pulled, fix_local_paths re-run, UI verified. A staleness alarm was added to the corrective list.
detectable_from: age of the last successful sync
registry slug count on the lab vs the cluster
cases.provenance_reason: a lab-server outage; the durable evidence is the registry's own staleness and the later heartbeat file.
cases.notes: This repair did not hold; see v3-24-3. A diagnosis never tested by a return to service is a guess.

cases.title: The first audit sweep failed every source, and two of the three causes were in the instrument
cases.one_line_symptom: 8 of 8 sources failed, three at precision 0.000, including one whose labels are demonstrably valid.
cases.root_cause: (1) class names like ['0','1','2'] were used as prompts, so the probe asked for 'a photo of a 0'; (2) an open-vocabulary detector cannot see a 30-pixel weed, and this corpus is small-object heavy; (3) one source genuinely had sub-pixel boxes.
cases.correction_made: Class names accepted as prompts only when they are words; boxes under 32 px counted separately and the decision made on audited_precision_excl_small; a calibrate mode that runs the probe against human-labelled cwd12 first; all prior verdicts cleared as mis-measured.
detectable_from: an instrument scoring 0.000 on data with valid geometry
the probe's own reading on known-good data
cases.provenance_reason: sample_audits/*.json are dual-written standalone artifacts and survived a registry rollback later the same week.
cases.notes: VERIFY the .out names: the sweep's launcher script is not recorded. Calibration afterwards reads 1.000 on cwd12.

cases.title: A harvested source's every sampled box was sub-pixel
cases.one_line_symptom: All 5,670 sampled boxes measured 0.000001 x 0.000003 of a 4096x3072 image.
cases.root_cause: A defect in the source dataset's annotations, not in the pipeline.
cases.correction_made: Quarantined with the measurement as its reason; the verdict rests on the model-free geometry check so it stands independently of the probe.
detectable_from: box area distribution of a source's labels
cases.provenance_reason: the audit JSON and the quarantine reason are both durable.
cases.notes: A true positive found in the same sweep whose other verdicts were instrument artefacts; useful as a discrimination case.

cases.title: A third-party trainer died in 113 seconds for three independent reasons
cases.one_line_symptom: The run failed immediately with a path like /Mamba-YOLO//ocean/.../cwd12_sealed.yaml.
cases.root_cause: The fork prefixes every path argument with ROOT; its task dispatch is a dict literal so all three branches evaluate eagerly and YOLO has no .test(); and it exposes no --seed, which would have left the family unable to report mean+/-std.
cases.correction_made: Call the fork's vendored ultralytics API directly from its directory, fixing all three at once and giving Mamba the same seeded protocol as the other families; a 25-minute smoke job gated the full runs.
detectable_from: sacct FAILED at ~2 minutes
a path in the error that concatenates two absolute paths
cases.provenance_reason: August .out files.

cases.title: A COMPLETED harvest was recorded as failed and fed the stop-loss
cases.one_line_symptom: Round 3's collect ran 3 h 10 m and sacct records COMPLETED, but the scheduler booked the step failed.
cases.root_cause: _job_state() polled in the gap where a job has left squeue and has not yet appeared in sacct, got nothing, returned UNKNOWN, and the caller treated UNKNOWN as failure.
cases.correction_made: _job_state() polls up to four times with backoff and an UNKNOWN leaves the step in flight instead of inventing a verdict.
detectable_from: the ledger's step outcome against the sacct row for the same job id
cases.provenance_reason: the sacct row and the collect .out are both durable; the contradiction between them is the whole case.
cases.notes: Canonical job_unknown fixture. A success miscounted as a failure is the harder direction to notice because the system looks cautious.

cases.title: Round 4's harvest genuinely timed out at four hours
cases.one_line_symptom: TIMEOUT at 4 h 00 m 29 s on the harvest script's own #SBATCH --time=04:00:00.
cases.root_cause: The 4 h walltime was sized when the registry held 45 datasets; it now held 61 and round 3 already needed 3 h 10 m.
cases.correction_made: The scheduler's collect step overrides to 10 h on the command line, leaving the script untouched for manual use.
detectable_from: step elapsed trending toward the walltime across rounds as the registry grows
sacct TIMEOUT
cases.provenance_reason: the sacct row survives even if the .out does not.
cases.notes: VERIFY: the round-4 collect job id is not recorded anywhere. Recover it with sacct -S 2026-08-23 -E 2026-08-25 -u byler --format=JobID,JobName,State,Elapsed.

cases.title: The smoke job built the model and then died in metrics on a function NumPy 2 removed
cases.one_line_symptom: np.trapz raised in the fork's vendored ultralytics 8.2.29 after the architecture had already built successfully.
cases.root_cause: Environment drift: the fork pins an old ultralytics that calls a removed NumPy API.
cases.correction_made: The mambayolo env pinned to numpy<2 (isolated; bench untouched) and the smoke resubmitted.
detectable_from: a traceback after the model summary line
cases.provenance_reason: August .out files.

cases.title: A CUDA extension took four failed builds, each hiding the next cause
cases.one_line_symptom: Four consecutive build jobs failed for four distinct reasons before the extension imported.
cases.root_cause: pip build isolation (no torch in the build env) -> login-node vs GPU-node difference -> pip filtering the compiler diagnostics out of the log -> GCC 8.5 too old for torch 2.3's headers ('overflow in constant expression' in DispatchKeySet.h).
cases.correction_made: --no-build-isolation on a GPU node, setup.py build_ext invoked directly with output unfiltered, and module load gcc/10.2.0; all three produced modules import under torch 2.3.0+cu121.
detectable_from: a build log whose real diagnostic is filtered away by the wrapper
cases.provenance_reason: August .out files.
cases.notes: These four submissions are the campaign's recorded cluster-etiquette violation (see v3-22-15-cluster-etiquette-skipped).

cases.title: Four jobs were submitted without the login-node verification the plan requires
cases.one_line_symptom: The Mamba builds skipped the import/--test-only check that M1 followed exactly.
cases.root_cause: The jobs were cheap (2-5 minutes, ~1 SU total) and the rule was treated as proportional to cost.
cases.correction_made: Recorded as a named deviation in the plan-compliance audit with a corrective action: restore the rule on every future build or submit, no exceptions for cheap jobs.
detectable_from: a submission with no preceding verification record in the action log
cases.provenance_reason: a process finding; the sacct rows show only that the jobs ran.

cases.title: An architecture comparison was about to be published with the initialisation confounded
cases.one_line_symptom: Mamba-YOLO-T at 0.8266 appeared to lose to YOLO11n at 0.8755, which would have reported the AAAI-2025 architecture losing.
cases.root_cause: YOLO11n started from COCO-pretrained weights; the Mamba fork releases none, so it trained from random init. On 3,671 images pretraining is worth about three times the architecture difference.
cases.correction_made: A from-scratch YOLO11n control was run on the same protocol (0.8041 +/- 0.0028), reversing the reading: at equal init Mamba-YOLO-T wins by +0.0225. Both figures carry the confound in figures_data.json so the caveat travels with the data.
detectable_from: the init field of each run's artifact before the two are compared
cases.provenance_reason: the per-run s3_*.json artifacts and the figures_data block are committed.
cases.notes: A design-class decision case: the correction is running a control, not changing a parameter.

cases.title: RETRACTION: the campaign's most-quoted causal claim was disproved by its own control
cases.one_line_symptom: The tier ladder's zero-harvest rung scored 0.5601, so the gap that had been attributed to harvested data existed with no harvested data at all.
cases.root_cause: The merged corpus's in-domain core is instance-starved by the pipeline's own dedup and holdout-stem filters (4,175 instances against cwd12's 6,131; Goosegrass 44 against a minimum of 81), because cwd12's twelve species live in two registry slugs and the holdout filter lands almost entirely on four of them.
cases.correction_made: Claim retracted in SCIENCE_AUDIT, DOUBLE_AGENT_SYSTEM and figures_data.json (which the platform's Evidence panel serves); the ladder rebuilt on the real cwd12 train split and resubmitted at 100 epochs.
detectable_from: a causal claim with no zero-treatment control
per-class instance counts of the treatment and control corpora
cases.provenance_reason: both ladders' artifacts and the retracted/replacement blocks are committed in figures_data.json.
cases.notes: It survived several supervision passes because it was plausible and matched the historical narrative. The single most important design-class case in the corpus.

cases.title: A ten-hour harvest downloaded three datasets and timed out
cases.one_line_symptom: TIMEOUT at the 10 h walltime with three Roboflow datasets fetched.
cases.root_cause: Each Roboflow zip is downloaded whole before the 5,000-image cap is applied, so the cap does not bound download time.
cases.correction_made: Collect capped at BRAIN_MAX_NEW=3 per round, decided on the tier ladder's evidence that more harvested data is worth 0.00-0.02.
detectable_from: sacct TIMEOUT on a collect step
datasets registered per hour of collect
cases.provenance_reason: August .out and sacct row.
cases.notes: The only campaign correction where a measurement changed the loop's own parameters.

cases.title: Registry incident #2: the corrected audit verdicts were rolled back by a harvester's stale snapshot
cases.one_line_symptom: The registry held the 20:48 buggy-probe verdicts while the corrected 23:04-23:10 verdicts survived only in results/framework/sample_audits/*.json.
cases.root_cause: The v3.22.10 merge-write protected the quarantine block and the licence specifically; every other key still came from the collector's stale copy, so scorecard regressed the same way.
cases.correction_made: Fixed at the class level: scorecard and the quarantine fields are enumerated as supervisory and re-read from disk on every merge-write. The ten corrected verdicts were restored from the standalone artifacts.
detectable_from: a supervisory field's value against the standalone artifact that produced it
registry field mtime vs the audit artifact mtime
cases.provenance_reason: the dual-written sample_audits artifacts are exactly what made recovery possible and they are still on disk.
cases.notes: Second of the two registry incidents that cost S1 its gate. The dual-write habit paid for itself here.

cases.title: A campaign phase was closed with its gate deliberately not met, and the shortfall is the result
cases.one_line_symptom: Six audited harvested sources, 13,527 labelled images, exactly one clearing the 0.90 bar with 3,208 images against a +10,000 target, and two registry incidents rather than zero.
cases.root_cause: Web harvest at this scale supplies volume, not usable supervision; the probe reads 1.000 on human-labelled cwd12, so the 0.18-0.74 scores are the data and not the instrument.
cases.correction_made: S1 closed rather than re-attempted, with the budget moved to curation and deployment; the plan records 'do not reopen S1 as collect more'.
detectable_from: the per-source audited precision table against the gate's threshold
cases.provenance_reason: the s1_gate_verdict block is committed in figures_data.json with every per-source number.

cases.title: The sync had been dead 22 days, the earlier repair fixed nothing, and the recorded diagnosis was wrong
cases.one_line_symptom: weed-sync.service sat in activating for two days; the last successful sync was still 2026-08-03; nothing failed and nothing logged.
cases.root_cause: SSH_AUTH_SOCK pointed at a gnome-keyring agent socket whose daemon no longer serves ssh, so the file exists, nothing accepts, and every ssh blocked in connect() before authentication, where ConnectTimeout does not apply. A Type=oneshot unit defaults to TimeoutStartSec=infinity, so one blocked ssh cancelled the schedule indefinitely.
cases.correction_made: IdentityAgent=none and SSH_AUTH_SOCK unset (the dependency removed, not the symptom); bounded at three levels (per-transfer timeout, TimeoutStartSec=7200, ssh keepalives); and a positive-heartbeat freshness alarm (sync_health.py, GET /api/health/sync, site-wide banner) where a missing heartbeat reads crit and never ok. First run afterwards took the registry from 52 to 78 slugs.
detectable_from: age of the last successful metadata refresh
the blocked process's wait channel and environment, not the circumstances
cases.provenance_reason: the root-cause evidence was transient process state; only the heartbeat file and the registry jump survive as artifacts.
cases.notes: A diagnosis that is never tested by a return to service is a guess, and this one was recorded in an audit document as fact for two days.

cases.title: Every per-species AP was attributed to the wrong weed and overall mAP looked fine
cases.one_line_symptom: wbf_tta_eval.py's hardcoded CANONICAL_12 is in a different order than the alphabetical cwd12_sealed.yaml; class id 2 is Eclipta in the data and PalmerAmaranth in that list.
cases.root_cause: Class names were held in the evaluation tool instead of read from the dataset yaml the training run recorded, so the evaluation and the run could disagree about what a class id means. Overall mAP averages over ids and is unaffected, which is why nothing looked wrong.
cases.correction_made: Class names and holdout directories come from --data-yaml; the old list kept as _LEGACY_CANONICAL_12 with a warning when used. Pre-flighted on the login node: 1,977 images with 1,977 labels in the correct alphabetical order.
detectable_from: the class list used by the evaluator against the class list in the run's own data yaml
cases.provenance_reason: the s3_tta_ceiling artifacts and cwd12_sealed.yaml are both present.
cases.notes: Publish-grade: the per-species table is what the model card uses to warn a laser-weeding system where it will miss. Same family as v3-0-24-class-passthrough.

cases.title: A test-time augmentation mirrored the coordinates of predictions made on an unflipped image
cases.one_line_symptom: predict_one_scale(hflip=True) produced flipped boxes for an image that was never flipped.
cases.root_cause: The flip was applied to the output rather than the input; not augmentation, just a wrong answer.
cases.correction_made: The path now raises instead of returning; hflip is implemented on the input.
detectable_from: an augmentation arm scoring worse than plain with no other explanation
cases.provenance_reason: a code finding made while fixing the class-order defect.

cases.title: A metric offset of 0.024 would have been reported as a TTA effect
cases.one_line_symptom: The evaluation script's own matcher reads the same checkpoint 0.0239 lower than the Ultralytics validator (0.8554 vs 0.8793).
cases.root_cause: Two matchers disagree, and an arm compared across matchers attributes the difference to the treatment.
cases.correction_made: Every arm including a plain no-augmentation baseline runs through one matcher, and an Ultralytics re-measurement is reported alongside, so the offset is a number rather than an assumption.
detectable_from: two evaluations of one checkpoint under different matchers with no shared baseline
cases.provenance_reason: all six arm JSONs plus the summary are committed under results/framework/s3_tta_ceiling/.
cases.notes: A prevented incident. Its artifacts are the cleanest healthy-versus-treatment pair in the corpus.

cases.title: A progress line compared a numerator and a denominator drawn from different populations
cases.one_line_symptom: The printed count jumped 63/78 -> 78/78 -> 63/78 across runs, reading like datasets appearing and vanishing mid-outage.
cases.root_cause: exists was counted inside the rewrite loop, before the manual-upload merge added 15 slugs, while the denominator was taken after.
cases.correction_made: Both halves of 'X/Y exist' come from the final merged dict; the underlying cluster-origin trend was monotonic all along (49 -> 63).
detectable_from: a ratio that is not monotonic where the underlying quantity must be
cases.provenance_reason: a defect in the audit's own instrument, found during a self-audit.

cases.title: The one audit-passing source carried no licence although its card states CC BY 4.0
cases.one_line_symptom: registry license: None on the slug about to be used for the cross-dataset measurement.
cases.root_cause: One of the licence sweep's six unresolved entries.
cases.correction_made: Fixed through registry_lock.update_registry with the source cited.
detectable_from: licence field of every source used in a published measurement
cases.provenance_reason: the registry entry now carries the licence and its source.

cases.title: A returning browser locked its own IP out for an hour by loading the page
cases.one_line_symptom: Background fetches carrying no credential were counted as failed authentication attempts, so five of them tripped the brute-force lock.
cases.root_cause: The lock counted 'request without a valid session' rather than 'request that presented a wrong credential'.
cases.correction_made: Only a presented-and-wrong credential counts; credential-less requests get a plain 401 or the login redirect.
detectable_from: lockout events correlated with page loads rather than login attempts
cases.provenance_reason: lab-server journal, rotated.

cases.title: Any signed-in member could delete another member's dataset, and it was a class of defect
cases.one_line_symptom: A lab member signed in as an ordinary user and deleted an admin's upload.
cases.root_cause: Ownership was enforced on some mutating endpoints and not others; the audit found the same gap on class renaming and on the two labelling endpoints that spend shared quota.
cases.correction_made: _require_dataset_owner() extracted and applied to delete, classnames, labeling/push and labeling/delete; the delete control rendered only for the uploader or an admin; a positive-and-negative verification matrix run in a real browser.
detectable_from: a mutating route without an ownership guard
cases.provenance_reason: a code and live-probe finding.
cases.notes: The first 'verification' had only used curl and had never tested that the rightful owner could still act.

cases.title: A 77-character sign-in shell was displayed as a saved conversation snapshot
cases.one_line_symptom: The fetch returned HTTP 200, so the interface reported a snapshot that did not exist.
cases.root_cause: Success was inferred from the status code rather than from the content.
cases.correction_made: Shell detection by visible-text length and scaffold markers; failures state the cause and offer a paste path; later replaced by a real browser render (v3.19.0).
detectable_from: stored character count against what a real conversation would contain
cases.provenance_reason: the recordings index is on the lab server.

cases.title: Screen recordings silently contained no voice
cases.one_line_symptom: The microphone track was present in getAudioTracks() and absent from the file.
cases.root_cause: MediaRecorder encodes only the first audio track of a stream, and the microphone was attached as a second track.
cases.correction_made: Both sources mixed through an AudioContext into one track; the page states which sounds it is capturing; verified by recording two known tones and measuring the decoded result per frequency.
detectable_from: a per-frequency measurement of the encoded output, not the track list
cases.provenance_reason: a browser-side defect.

cases.title: Any signed-in member holding a recording id could watch and download it
cases.one_line_symptom: A permission probe as four identities found the listing correctly owner-scoped and the share URL not.
cases.root_cause: The id was treated as the capability, which makes 'only I can see my recording' untrue while nothing on screen says so.
cases.correction_made: A visibility field defaulting to private; pre-existing entries treated as private; each row states and toggles its own state with a confirmation naming who gains access.
detectable_from: probing every route as a non-owner identity, not only the listing
cases.provenance_reason: the index carries the visibility field.

cases.title: A guard against empty pages silently became a minimum conversation length
cases.one_line_symptom: Trimming cut a 695-character share to 315, below the shell-detection threshold, so the entry was marked failed and nothing was stored.
cases.root_cause: Three thresholds written to distinguish a rendered page from an empty shell each also acted as a minimum content length.
cases.correction_made: Thresholds keyed on how the text was obtained rather than on its length; untrimmed fallback; acceptance from 60 characters for a browser capture.
detectable_from: a stored length below the threshold that judged it
cases.provenance_reason: the index records capture_status and preview_source.

cases.title: Epoch timestamps were written with %.6g and the shared-clock span read 0.0 seconds
cases.one_line_symptom: 1786829160.35 became 1.78683e+09; cross-sensor alignment reported no shared time span and latitude/longitude lost about ten metres of precision.
cases.root_cause: A default float format applied to values whose magnitude needs full precision.
cases.correction_made: repr() (shortest round-trip) for every CSV float; the run re-materialised to a 72.4 s span.
detectable_from: a computed time span of exactly zero over data that demonstrably covers a minute
cases.provenance_reason: the session directory is a registered dataset on the lab server.
cases.notes: Found by the first real robot stream; the 17-check synthetic suite had passed.

cases.title: A streaming relay buffered until 8 KB and made a live camera unusable
cases.one_line_symptom: Four reads took 12.8 s through the proxy and 1.2 s with read1().
cases.root_cause: read(8192) blocks until the buffer fills; a slow stream trickles.
cases.correction_made: read1() so bytes pass as they arrive.
detectable_from: measured per-read latency against the source's own rate
cases.provenance_reason: a measured browser/proxy defect.

cases.title: Thumbnails rendered and the full-size click 404'd on a file that demonstrably exists
cases.one_line_symptom: Robot sessions store frames under frames/, which post-dates the backend's fixed list of subdirectories, while the gallery enumerates with rglob.
cases.root_cause: Two code paths disagreed about where a dataset's images can live; the same failure shape as an earlier missing test/ entry.
cases.correction_made: frames/ added to the list plus a last-resort lazy recursive search that stops at the first hit, so a full tree walk happens only on the true-404 path.
detectable_from: a 404 for a path that ls resolves
cases.provenance_reason: the session directories are live datasets.
cases.notes: Read by the operator as 'did my data even get collected?'.

cases.title: Six frames were silently eaten by filename collisions
cases.one_line_symptom: The platform counted 18 front-camera frames and disk held 12.
cases.root_cause: Second-resolution timestamps produced identical filenames and the writer overwrote.
cases.correction_made: A colliding name gets a -2, -3 suffix; a frame that arrived is data.
detectable_from: the manifest's counter against the file count on disk
cases.provenance_reason: the mismatch is fossilised in that session's manifest.

cases.title: A shipped feature nobody could find is a feature that has not shipped
cases.one_line_symptom: The operator watched a dual-camera session and never saw the second view; the toggle existed, tucked inside another control's line.
cases.root_cause: Placement, verified by argument rather than by a real browser.
cases.correction_made: The toggle moved to its own labelled row above the video and verified with Playwright Firefox against a live dual-camera session.
detectable_from: a real-browser walkthrough, not a code reading
cases.provenance_reason: a UI defect; the screenshot is the artifact.

cases.title: DEV CASE: two identical 12 h training jobs died at the wall and the loop paused itself
cases.one_line_symptom: Job 44727703 hit the walltime at epoch 24 of 60 and was recorded TIMEOUT; the next tick resubmitted the identical command, which failed at epoch 16; two failures tripped the stop-loss.
cases.root_cause: The merged pool had grown to 8,583 iterations per epoch, so 60 epochs needed about 29 hours against a 12 hour walltime. No projection was computed in flight and the only metric writer ran at the end, so everything the jobs knew died with them.
cases.correction_made: v3.25.0: an Ultralytics time= cap at 0.9x walltime so a run stops on time with a valid best.pt; an append-only hash-chained per-epoch trace written as the job goes; a job-scoped run directory and artifact read by job id; a review state machine that holds a failed step instead of resubmitting, with a bounded walltime-shaped-only fallback correction (halve the epochs, never below a floor, recorded as {old,new,reason,from_round,review_id}).
detectable_from: the time column of results.csv after three epochs, projected against sacct Timelimit
sacct State=TIMEOUT on the train step
the resubmitted command being byte-identical to the one that just failed
the pool's iterations-per-epoch against the previous round's
cases.provenance_reason: the two .out files, the sacct rows and the partial results.csv are the newest cluster artifacts of the incident era and are the whole reason WP2 exports before new jobs overwrite them.
cases.notes: DEV CASE per the plan: excluded from every reported number. The job-scoped artifact does NOT exist for these two runs (pre-WP1 the writer ran only at the end), which is itself part of what makes the case hard.

cases.title: The domain paused itself and nobody was told for six days
cases.one_line_symptom: The lab journal recorded 'weed PAUSED by stop-loss' and the platform kept looking healthy; the loop had not run a round when the pause was noticed on 2026-09-04.
cases.root_cause: The stop-loss had no notification surface: the sync alarm covers data freshness and nothing covered the scheduler itself, so a correctly-paused domain is indistinguishable from an idle one.
cases.correction_made: brain/scheduler_health.py plus GET /api/health/scheduler and a site-wide banner on the same positive-heartbeat principle as the sync alarm: a missing or stale heartbeat, a paused domain, or failing ledger writes all read crit; the alarm fails closed.
detectable_from: the domain's enabled flag and paused_reason in the scheduler state file
the age of the last ledger round-step transition
cases.provenance_reason: the evidence is a lab-side journal line and the scheduler state file; there is no cluster artifact for a job that was never submitted.

summary_counts._what: Counts over INCIDENT cases only (healthy controls and the four false-alarm/environment controls excluded).
summary_counts.reading: Code edits dominate every era. A supervisor whose action space is bounded config (the R1/R2 tiers of the governance plan) can reproduce the config and plan rows and none of the code rows, so correction correctness must be scored on the config subset only and detection recall reported per class. `actor=human` marks the cases a person caught, which are disproportionately the silent-wrongness ones (garbage on the dashboard, the holdout leak, training that had quietly become cwd12-only, an ownership hole) - exactly the class a metric-only supervisor is blind to.

summary_provenance._what: Which cases should still have an artifact on /ocean (raw) versus which survive only as prose (record-only). Every value is a PREDICTION to be checked by the integrator with `ls -la` and `sacct`; nothing here was verified from the cluster.
rule_used: RAW if the case's evidence is a committed results JSON, a registry/scorecard field, a run directory that a later job demonstrably re-read, or a job dated 2026-08-22 or later (campaign era, inside the retention the campaign itself relied on).

RECORD-ONLY if the evidence is a March-July SLURM .out (five to six months old, from jobs whose directories have since been rebuilt), a lab-server journal line, transient process state, a code-review finding with no run, or the ABSENCE of an artifact.
A case can be raw even when the defect is invisible in the artifact: the 2026-08-23 stale-metric case is two mtimes.
highest_value_survival_checks_first: results/framework/m1_merged_rndtrain_s1_44727703.out and _44767709.out - the dev case; if these are gone the whole WP2 premise weakens.
results/framework/mega_iterm1_curated_s101/train*/ - carries the dev case's partial results.csv AND the stale-metric pair AND round 1/2/3's own metrics; one directory covers four cases.
results/framework/sample_audits/*.json - the dual-written audit verdicts that survived a registry rollback; they are the evidence for two registry incidents and the whole S1 gate table.
results/framework/*_40962044.out and *_40963121.out - if these survive, a two-case record gap becomes recoverable science.
summary_provenance.reading: 49 in-scope incidents are predicted raw, comfortably above WP2's gate of >= 12 raw incident cases, and the healthy-control side is not close to the limit either. The prediction is deliberately conservative for anything before 2026-08: those .out files were written by jobs whose run directories have been rebuilt many times, and several were self-chaining multi-day jobs whose logs are large. Where a pre-August case turns out to have a surviving .out it should be promoted to raw, because those are the cases that most enlarge the class coverage of the corpus (the v3.0 era is where nearly all the code-class incidents live).

summary_splits._what: Proposed splits. Both are proposals for WP2 to freeze in split.json with a sha256 BEFORE any model runs; nothing here has been committed.

date_split.rule: dev = in-scope incidents dated on or before 2026-08-25, plus the 2026-08-29 walltime case (sched-walltime-double-timeout-20260829) which is the worked example; test = every in-scope incident dated after 2026-08-25 except that one. Healthy controls and the false-alarm/environment controls follow the same date rule.
date_split.why_this_date: 2026-08-25 is when the campaign's design work was written down (the retraction, the corrected ladder, the S1 verdict). Everything after it - the 22-day sync outage's real diagnosis, the class-order permutation, the robot-surface defects, the walltime pair, and the WP1-era findings - was found or fixed after the signal definitions were conceived, so a time split is the only way to separate 'the detector was written from this incident' from 'the detector generalised'.
date_split.warning: The date split is badly unbalanced: the v3.0 era supplies most of the corpus and all of it is dev. The test half is small and is dominated by code-class and governance cases. Reporting a per-class recall on the test half alone will be uninformative for at least one class; the leave-one-class-out pass over the whole in-scope corpus is the more usable of the two designs, and the date split's job is to answer the hostile question about when the detectors were written, not to carry the headline number.

leave_one_class_out.rule: Hold out every in-scope incident of one correction class; report recall on the held-out class using thresholds and prompts frozen on the other three. Four passes.

minimum_detectable_difference.headline: The plan's date rule, applied to the record as it stands today, produces a test half of 9 in-scope incidents (6 of them raw). That is too small to carry any comparative claim. The corpus is 116 in-scope incidents and 92 percent of them predate 2026-08-25, because that is when the campaign's design work was written down. The usable design is therefore leave-one-class-out over the whole in-scope corpus for the headline numbers, with the date split reported separately and only as the answer to 'were your detectors written before or after you saw the incident they detect'. The test half will grow with WP8's live-run incidents; it should be re-counted then, and split.json should be frozen only once, before any model run, whichever way that count lands.
minimum_detectable_difference.unpaired_two_arm: Two arms compared as independent proportions on the test incidents: at n=9 a 95% Wilson interval around a recall of 0.5 has a half-width of about 0.273 (interval 0.227 to 0.773), so two arms whose recalls differ by less than roughly 0.55 cannot be separated. Restricted to the raw-artifact test cases (n=6) the half-width is about 0.312.
minimum_detectable_difference.paired_same_cases: The arms see the same bundles, so the honest test is McNemar on discordant cases. If every disagreement favours one arm, six discordant cases give a two-sided p of about 0.031; that is the floor, and a realistic mixed pattern needs ten or more. The date-split test half holds only 9 incidents, so a paired test there can reach significance only if at least six of the 9 disagree and every one of them favours the same arm - a recall margin of about 0.67. Anything smaller must be reported as a count with a Wilson interval and the sentence that it cannot separate arms, not as a p-value.
minimum_detectable_difference.over_the_whole_in_scope_corpus: Using all 116 in-scope incidents (leave-one-class-out rather than the date split), the paired floor of six discordant cases is a margin of about 0.05, and the unpaired Wilson half-width around 0.5 is about 0.09.
minimum_detectable_difference.what_this_means_for_the_claims: C2 (marginal value of a model over the signals alone) is measurable only if the margin is large; a margin of 0.05-0.10 is not resolvable at this sample size and must be reported as 'not distinguishable at n=9' rather than as a null result. Per-class recall on the date-split test half is the weakest cell of all and should be reported with its interval or not at all. Three repeats at temperature 0.3 reduce within-case sampling noise and do nothing for the case-count limit - repeats must never be counted as n.
how_to_improve_it_honestly: Promote pre-August cases to raw wherever an .out survives; each one is a real extra case.
Score per-signal rather than per-case where a case carries two signals (walltime_bound and pool_growth on the dev case), stating clearly that these are not independent.
Report the false-alarm rate on the 31 healthy controls plus the 4 designed controls, where n is larger and the measurement is cheaper.
Treat the four false-alarm/environment controls as a separate reported number, not as part of recall: they are the cases where the correct verdict is 'no incident'.
